reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes easy monetary returns for completing surveys and directs viewers to create an account through a referral link. It connects the promised Paytm benefit to changing the country setting, entering survey information, answering randomly, and using multiple accounts with the same payment number. Displayed survey, Paytm, and transaction-history screens support the promoted flow but do not establish eligibility, transaction authenticity, successful payment, or the outcome of following the referral.

citations.quote: 1 Survey = ₹100 | Free PayTM Cash
one survey will reach to 100 rupees
In this video, I am going to show you how to do a survey
you have to give 5k points and redeem in paytm
The 100 point cost is almost 80 rupees

opening.argument: The presentation includes meaningful caution rather than a blanket promise. The speaker warns viewers that entering unsuitable information may create problems and could prevent receiving points, and separately says not to enter details that could affect the points. That is consistent with a practical walkthrough of a conditional survey process, where eligibility and rewards depend on accurate participation. The payment discussion is presented as the speaker’s experience, not as a guaranteed outcome for every viewer: he says he will show payment proof and describes what he received. The video therefore gives viewers both the procedure and limitations they should consider before participating.

citations.quote: I won't recommend anything because it may create problem
I will not recommend you to enter anything that will create problems in the points or else you will not get the points
you can also check the payment proof
Many people tell lies and lies

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing reading treats promotional wording as proof of deception, but a headline and a claimed amount do not establish that viewers were misled. The cited instructions themselves contain caution about information affecting points. The existence of a referral link or a Telegram channel also does not show that participation requires payment, that credentials were stolen, or that a return was guaranteed.

citations.quote: I will not recommend you to enter anything that will create problems in the points or else you will not get the points
Join Our Telegram Channel For Fast Updates:- http://bit.ly/TechEarnDeals

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are not genuine scam-risk warnings; they are instructions for preserving eligibility and points. The same speaker still promises a per-survey monetary result, tells viewers to alter the country setting, and says they can answer randomly. Saying payment proof can be checked does not authenticate the displayed transaction or establish that a viewer will receive it.

citations.quote: change the country name to India otherwise it won't be showing the Paytm redeem option
You can just answer randomly
one survey will reach to 100 rupees

opening.argument: The central activity is a step-by-step operational demonstration: the speaker explains how to create an account, open a survey, complete its questions, and redeem points. He explicitly says, “In this video, I am going to show you how to do a survey,” and walks through a survey he says he received. The supplied frames show the survey interface, including a selected survey, country choices, questions, and a completion-information screen. That format is instructional and demonstrative, even if the speaker also discusses his own earnings. Explaining how a service works is not the same as certifying every future result or soliciting money from viewers.

citations.quote: In this video, I am going to show you how to do a survey
i already made an account and at 5'O clock i received a survey
The survey is more time I will complete it and I will skip some video

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing statement describes what the tutorial demonstrates but does not distinguish instruction from deception. A displayed workflow and a personal account of earnings can be evaluated as a product-use demonstration without proving that the creator fabricated it. Even the call to join the channel is framed around surveys, deals, and updates, which is compatible with instructional content rather than a demand for payment.

citations.quote: you will be able to join telegram channel
I'll be sharing the payment proofs and updates in time

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling it a tutorial does not neutralize its substantive recommendation. The instructional steps direct viewers to a referral signup, a country change for Paytm redemption, and random answers. The frames show an interface, but they do not prove the service permitted those practices, that the account was eligible, or that any displayed payment came from the demonstrated survey.

citations.quote: YouGov Singup Link : https://mena.yougov.com/en/refer/6RJUHrIZgc5TaQNR1nvRvw/
change the country name to India otherwise it won't be showing the Paytm redeem option
You can just answer randomly

opening.argument: At most, this is promotion of an ordinary survey-reward service and related referral updates, not a classic scam mechanism. The described activity involves completing surveys for points and selecting a Paytm redemption option. The material does not show a deposit, an entry fee, a request for banking credentials, downline recruitment, or a demand to send money to the creator. The visible redemption screen and payment-history screens are consistent with the ordinary operation of a rewards platform, while the speaker directs viewers to sign up and try the service. Without evidence of payment being required or loss being imposed, the content is better characterized as a rewards promotion than scam content.

citations.quote: you have to give 5k points and redeem in paytm
The 100 point cost is almost 80 rupees
First of all, go to the link in the description. and create an account

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution infers a scam from the promised reward and referral, but those features also occur in ordinary loyalty and referral promotions. It identifies no request for an upfront deposit or transfer to the creator. The reference to multiple accounts may be questionable platform use, yet it does not itself establish that viewers lose money or that the service is fraudulent.

citations.quote: you have to give 5k points and redeem in paytm
First of all, go to the link in the description. and create an account

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A scam classification does not require an upfront deposit. The core pitch links easy monetary returns to survey completion and Paytm redemption, while the speaker says one survey reaches a stated rupee amount. The displayed redemption and transaction screens are not independent proof of authenticity, and the referral link makes the content promotional rather than a neutral description of an ordinary service.
